title: The Second Flare
hook: Dad's rule for a night breakdown: light one flare. And if you ever see a second one down the road... lock the doors.
lines: My dad kept a box of road flares in my trunk... and one rule, taped inside the lid.
If you break down at night, light one flare behind the car. Just one.
And if you ever see a second flare down the road... lock the doors. Don't wave for help.
Last winter, my car died on an empty mountain road, an hour past midnight.
I lit one flare, set it behind the bumper, and climbed back inside to wait for the tow truck.
For twenty minutes... nothing. Just snow, and that red light hissing in the mirror.
Then, far down the road behind me... a second flare lit up.
I locked the doors. I didn't wave.
A minute later, a third flare lit. Closer.
Then a fourth. Close enough to see the snow falling around it... and nobody standing there.
Then, one by one... they all went out.
When the tow truck finally came, the driver found me curled up on the back seat.
He walked around with his flashlight, opened my trunk... and asked why my flare box was empty.
Dad always packs six. I'd only taken one.
